steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three high-impact strategies cities can use to cut carbon emissions:

1. Accelerate low-carbon mobility  
   • Expand and prioritize high-quality public transit (bus rapid transit, light rail)  
   • Build safe, connected cycling and walking networks  
   • Incentivize electric vehicles (charging infrastructure, preferential parking) and implement car-free or congestion-priced zones  

2. Retrofit and green our building stock  
   • Launch large-scale energy-efficiency retrofit programs (insulation, high-efficiency glazing, LED lighting)  
   • Switch heating and cooling systems to low-carbon alternatives (heat pumps, district heating using waste heat or renewables)  
   • Enforce “zero-carbon” building codes for all new construction  

3. Deploy local clean energy and smart grids  
   • Facilitate rooftop and community solar installations, small wind or geothermal projects  
   • Invest in energy storage (batteries, pumped hydro) to smooth renewable output  
   • Implement smart-grid technologies and demand-response programs so supply and demand balance in real time  

Together, these measures tackle emissions from transport, buildings, and power—responsible for the lion’s share of urban carbon footprints.
